meta.title: Bookguardian — a home for the books you own
meta.description: Bookguardian keeps track of the books on your shelves: where each one lives, who borrowed it, what you made of it and when you finished it. Mobile-first, installable and self-hostable.

hero.title: Every book you own, on the shelf where you left it
hero.body: Scan a cover, drop the book on a shelf, and Bookguardian remembers the rest: what you have read, what you are reading, and who still has your copy.
hero.shot: The Bookguardian library screen on a phone: libraries with their shelf and book counts.

shelves.title: Libraries and shelves
shelves.body: Books live in a library and on a shelf. A new install already has one of each, so adding a book asks you nothing.

scan.title: Scan to add
scan.body: Point the camera at a barcode, or read the cover with OCR, and the add form arrives already filled in.

search.title: Search while you type
search.body: Fill in what you remember, search Open Library and Google Books from the form, and pick the right edition.

covers.title: Covers, automatically
covers.body: Covers are found, resized and cached on your own server, with a readable placeholder when there is nothing to find.

reading.title: Reading life
reading.body: To read, reading or read; zero to five stars; and the date you turned the last page.

lending.title: Lending
lending.body: Who has which book, since when, when it is due back, and what is already overdue.

stats.title: Statistics
stats.body: Counts by library, shelf, category and status, plus a timeline of what you finished and when.

mobile.title: Built for one thumb
mobile.body: A mobile-first PWA you can install: full screen, readable offline, dark mode since day one.

ownership.title: Your library is yours
ownership.body: Sign in with Google, one account per email, your data kept apart from everyone else's, and deletable whenever you want.

selfhost.title: Self-hostable
selfhost.body: A single Docker container with SQLite on a volume. Run it on your own box and nothing leaves it.
